notesStmt.note: Whitman contemplated writing an essay about Elias Hicks for many years. While finishing preparations for the printing of November Boughs, Whitman told Horace Traubel, "Some of these bits were written as many as thirty years ago. Some of them I have written within the past year. They are a miscellaneous lot but they all belong in the same stream" (see Traubel, With Walt Whitman in Camden, 2:42). It is therefore difficult to determine the exact date of the present manuscript. Although the significance of the dates written on the reverse is unclear, the manuscript was likely created in or after 1875, the most recent year listed there.

note.p: Whitman used these brief notes on the reigns of Frederick the Great (Prussia) and King George III (Great Britain) in the opening paragraph of "Elias Hicks, Notes (such as they are)," an essay first published in November Boughs (1888).
